## Historical audit: S0095

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/replay_s1_r1/M_descendant/C1/replay_selection/commons_29206714/trajectory.jsonl`. Only supplied chunk 3 of 3 is audited; image paths are recorded, but their pixels are not visible here.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Line 22, student `model_request`, characters [0,271079) | The assigned goal was an editable, single-photo indoor reconstruction with matching camera, geometry and materials. The student’s interpretation was a country kitchen with dresser, open doors, crockery, fireplace, swift and foreground spinning wheel. Those labels and estimated anchors are hypotheses, not independent identification of the reference. |
| Line 22, embedded student programs | The first build defines multiple separately owned objects and components, including door hinges, wheel spokes and supports. It assigns colors and a procedural wood-grain shader, camera, world and area lights. This establishes intended construction and materials, not verified physical contact, connections, texture appearance or reference fidelity. |
| Line 22, embedded step 1–2 exchange | The student reported a too-small crown, overly broad wheel and mantel/door overlap. It then increased lens 52→64 and camera height, changed the wheel plane and moved the wheel owner, moved the fireplace and changed swift rods. Step 2 reported `ok: true`. These simultaneous changes prevent attributing any visual effect to one intervention. |
| Line 22, embedded step 2–3 exchange | The student judged shelf/crown slopes inconsistent and hypothesized the camera was on the wrong side; it moved the camera across the scene and changed wheel angle and position, retaining lens 64. Step 3 reported `ok: true`. The wheel’s owner was raised, but ground contact and part connections were not tested. |
| Line 22, embedded runner feedback; lines 23–25, characters [0,4410), [0,366), [0,59) | All three builds were reported successful, with rendered PNG and blend-save logs. The final read-only selection session had four images supplied and zero tool calls; the student answered `SELECT 2`, and a `select` event recorded step 2. This is a formal selection of a technically successful build, **not independent visual or geometric verification**. |

**Teacher input and autonomy.** No separate teacher diagnosis, proposed update, or receipt is visible in this chunk. The embedded system and runner supplied reconstruction and review instructions; the student demonstrably received them and made its own revisions within the fixed interface. No independent external exploration is evidenced; the selection session disabled shell, browser and other tools.

**Uncertainty and lessons.** Camera-side diagnosis, wheel pose, fireplace occlusion, object inventory, material appearance and lighting quality remain unverified without the images or geometric checks. There is no visible render failure, empty patch or technical interruption; overall reconstruction correctness is **unknown**, despite successful execution and selection. Transferably, separate ownership enables coherent object edits, while changing multiple parameter families at once makes causal assessment difficult. The particular camera and wheel adjustments are task-specific hypotheses, not general correction rules.
